license_required.quote: no person shall practice medicine or surgery in the State, either gratuitously or for pay, or offer to practice medicine or surgery in the State, or advertise or announce one's self, either publicly or privately, as prepared or qualified to practice medicine or surgery in the State, or append the letters "Dr.", "M.D.", or "D.O." to one's name with the intent to imply that the person is a practitioner of medicine or surgery, without having a valid unrevoked license or a limited and temporary license obtained from the Hawaii medical board.

type.quote: The board shall consist of eleven persons, seven of whom shall be physicians or surgeons licensed under the laws of the State, two of whom shall be osteopathic physicians licensed under the laws of the State, and two of whom shall be lay members appointed from the public at large.

interval_years.quote: Every physician or surgeon holding a license under this chapter shall renew the license with the board no later than January 31 of each even-numbered year.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Procuring, or aiding or abetting in procuring, an unlawful abortion
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Procuring, or aiding or abetting in procuring, an abortion that is unlawful under the laws of this State

disciplinary_grounds.description: Employing any person to solicit patients for oneself
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Employing any person to solicit patients for one's self

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in false, fraudulent, or deceptive advertising
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Engaging in false, fraudulent, or deceptive advertising, including but not limited to: (A) Making excessive claims of expertise in one or more medical specialty fields; (B) Assuring a permanent cure for an incurable disease; or (C) Making any untruthful and improbable statement in advertising one's medical or surgical practice or business

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being habituated to excessive use of drugs or alcohol or addicted to a narcotic or similar drug
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Being habituated to the excessive use of drugs or alcohol; or being addicted to, dependent on, or a habitual user of a narcotic, barbiturate, amphetamine, hallucinogen, or other drug having similar effects

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing medicine while ability to practice is impaired by alcohol, drugs, physical disability, or mental instability

disciplinary_grounds.description: Professional misconduct, hazardous negligence causing bodily injury, or manifest incapacity in the practice of medicine or surgery

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction, whether by nolo contendere or otherwise, of a penal offense substantially related to the qualifications, functions, or duties of a physician or osteopathic physician

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of chapter 329, the uniform controlled substances act, or any rule adopted thereunder
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violation of chapter 329, the uniform controlled substances act, or any rule adopted thereunder except as provided in section 329-122

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to report to the board any disciplinary decision issued against the licensee in another jurisdiction within thirty days

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: A foreign medical school and has had at least two years of residency in a program accredited by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education or the American Osteopathic Association...and: (i) Holds the national certificate of the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates, or its successor

pain_management_education_required.quote: The Hawaii medical board may establish guidelines for physicians or osteopathic physicians with respect to patients' pain management.

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: For purposes of prescribing opiates via telehealth, a physician-patient relationship shall only be established after an in-person consultation between the prescribing physician and the patient.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: For the purposes of prescribing opiates or certifying a patient for the medical use of cannabis, a physician-patient relationship shall only be established after an in-person consultation between the prescribing physician and the patient.

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: Treatment recommendations via telehealth, including issuing prescriptions electronically, are held to the same standards as traditional physician-patient settings. Issuing a prescription based solely on an online questionnaire is not acceptable. For opiates or cannabis certification, an in-person consultation is required first.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: Treatment recommendations made via telehealth, including issuing a prescription via electronic means, shall be held to the same standards of appropriate practice as those in traditional physician-patient settings that do not include [an] in-person visit but in which prescribing is appropriate, including on-call telephone encounters and encounters for which a follow-up visit is arranged. Issuing a prescription based solely on an online questionnaire is not treatment for the purposes of this section and does not constitute an acceptable standard of care. For the purposes of prescribing opiates or certifying a patient for the medical use of cannabis, a physician-patient relationship shall only be established after an in-person consultation between the prescribing physician and the patient.

telemedicine_license_available.quote: Subject to section 453-2(b), nothing in this section shall preclude any physician acting within the scope of the physician's license to practice from practicing telehealth as defined in this section.

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: The board shall establish the degree of supervision required by the supervising physician, osteopathic physician, or group of physicians when a physician assistant performs a service within the practice of medicine.

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: Physician assistants may prescribe controlled substances subject to supervision requirements; supervising physician must review at least 50% of controlled substance prescription records during first year of PA practice.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: For physician assistants who issue controlled substance prescriptions, at least fifty per cent of the records reviewed under clause (i) or (ii) shall include controlled substance prescriptions

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: Every physician or osteopathic physician licensed pursuant to this chapter who does not possess professional liability insurance shall report any settlement or arbitration award of a claim or action for damages for death or personal injury caused by negligence, error, or omission in practice, or the unauthorized rendering of professional services.

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: Where the board has reasonable cause to believe that a licensee is or may be unable to practice medicine with reasonable skill and safety to protect patients, the board may order the licensee to submit to a mental or physical examination or any combination thereof, by a licensed practitioner approved by the board, at the licensee's expense.
